quotes.quote: you can use Vercel or Railway for ease of use
quotes.excerpt: For apps at scale, you can use Vercel or Railway for ease of use. I prefer to use Cloudflare pages/workers and a DigitalOcean droplet or something. Putting it up in standard cloud infrastructure also forces you to think a little bit more about how it’s built. E.g. where does the database live? Is there a separate API service, or built-in? Thinking like that will help your app perform better already at scale, instead
quotes.story: Ask HN: Deployed vibecoded apps in prod at scale?

quotes.quote: I was paying Vercel $20 per month for serving static pages(it’s 4 times more than I pay Railway for the Postgres database
quotes.excerpt: I migrated the landing pages for my app[1] from Nextjs to Astrojs mainly because I was paying Vercel $20 per month for serving static pages(it’s 4 times more than I pay Railway for the Postgres database for the actual app and also 4 times more than I pay Cloudflare for hosting all my apps). I used AI for migrating and it took a few days only as the existing repo was used as “instructions” and it included some upgrade
quotes.story: We moved Railway's front end off Next.js. Builds went from 10 minutes to under 2
